summary: This defines a RobotPet class that stores a pet's name, battery level, and mood, and gives it a show_talent method that returns a short description of a trick. It is the class the unit tests in this chapter will check.

lines.text: Starts the blueprint for a robot pet; every pet created from it gets the same attributes and methods.
The constructor runs automatically whenever a new RobotPet is created, and it demands the three starting values.
Stores the name on the object itself so it survives after the constructor finishes.
Keeps the battery level as part of the pet's state; later tests will change and check this value.
Records the pet's mood, the third piece of state that makes each robot pet distinct.
Defines the behaviour under test. It is deliberately generic here so that subclasses can override it later.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} performs a generic trick!"
lines.text: Returning the sentence instead of printing it is what makes the method testable: a test can compare the returned string against an expected one.
